name: FlashAttention
notes: Streaming online-softmax flash-attention NKI kernel (never materializes [S,S]). Layout q,k,v=(d_head,seqlen), out=(seqlen,d_head), UNSCALED scores. Single-head entries: flash_fwd (bf16 non-causal), flash_fwd_fp32, flash_fwd_causal. BATCHED entry flash_fwd_batched (via adapter:build_flash_batched_forward): q,k,v=(BH,d_head,seqlen), out=(BH,seqlen,d_head), one dispatch loops the B*H heads on-device. CALIBRATION (2026-08-28, single trn2 core, hd=128, fresh-input steady-state): SINGLE-head dense attention is COMPILER-STRONG - the compiler beats/ties this kernel S=8k-32k and does not OOM through 65k, so single-head is NOT worth authoring. The WIN is BATCHED-MULTI-HEAD long-context: dense [B,H,S,S] OOMs (NCC_EOOM001, >24GB HBM) at B8/H16/S8192 (~34GB fp32 scores) while flash_fwd_batched RAN - flash is the ONLY path there. At B8/H32/S4096 (17GB, dense tiles+fits) batched flash ~ties dense and beats SDPA. So this kernel is a real win ONLY above the dense-OOM boundary (opportunity.py flags it via B*H*S*S >= ~6e9). bf16 tracks the incumbent to ~1e-2. Invoked output-as-arg via torch_neuronx.nki_jit. NOTE: the batched head-loop unrolls (affine_range) so compile time grows with B*H.
